raw_segments.text: A portion of the tastes and of the habits of the aristocracy may consequently be discovered
in the characters of men in the profession of the law.
They participate in the same instinctive love of order and of formalities, and they entertain
the same repugnance to the actions of the multitude and the same secret contempt of
I do not mean to say that the natural propensities of lawyers are sufficiently strong to sway
them irresistibly, for they, like most other men, are governed by their private interests
and the advantages of the moment.
